correctness.rationale: Schwab–Thompson Proposition 1.1 supplies an iff sorted-prefix test for sums of distinct divisor-aliquot values. For composite n, each distinct prime divisor contributes one weight s(p)=1, other composite divisors have s(d)>=3. Exhausting the exponent partitions of Omega(n) in {2,3,4} constrains possible p^a and p^a q^b forms, leaving n=12,24,36,60,84,90,100,126,198. Checking the exact sorted positive weights excludes all except 60; s(60) multiset sorted is [1,1,1,3,6,8,9,16,22,42,108] and satisfies every prefix inequality. No unbounded enumeration cutoff is used. Independent factorization/subset-prefix check through n=100000 corroborated the symbolic partition proof.
residual_risks: The proof classifies only the first composite Omega-layer, not all composite s-practical integers.
Case lists depend on the exact aliquot formula sigma(d)-d and positive-multiset convention with s(1)=0 omitted.
